definitions.explanation: A condensed version of a text, speech, or argument that presents the key points. Used in academic, business, and everyday contexts when distilling information to its essentials.

examples.japanese: {記事|きじ}の{要約|ようやく}を{書|か}く。
examples.english: I write a summary of the article.

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}の{内容|ないよう}を{要約|ようやく}してください。
examples.english: Please summarize the contents of the meeting.

examples.japanese: {論文|ろんぶん}の{冒頭|ぼうとう}には{要約|ようやく}をつけるのが{一般的|いっぱんてき}だ。
examples.english: It is standard to include an abstract at the beginning of an academic paper.

notes:
USAGE:
Do not confuse {要約|ようやく} (summary) with the adverb {漸|ようや}く (finally, at last), which is a homophone with a completely different meaning and kanji. {要約|ようやく} can be used as a noun or as a する verb meaning "to summarize."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {要約|ようやく}する: to summarize
- {要約|ようやく}を{書|か}く: to write a summary
- {要約|ようやく}{文|ぶん}: summary text
- {要約|ようやく}{力|りょく}: summarization ability
- {三行|さんぎょう}{要約|ようやく}: three-line summary (internet slang for TL;DR)
